newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli parliament to get budget cuts this week.
newsitem.headline: Israeli parliament to get budget cuts this week.

text.p: Israel's Treasury expects to send the second round of cuts it proposes for the 1997 budget to parliament by the end of this week, Treasury officials said on Monday.

They said agreements had been reached on line-item cuts with all the ministries except interior ministry. The reductions range from 0.5 percent for the defence ministry to five percent for the Treasury and prime minister's office.

The reductions total 1.2 billion shekels ($365.9 million) and come on top of the 4.9 billion shekels in cuts contained in the original 1997 budget. In addition, the Treasury plans to raise 600 million shekels through new, non-tax sources, such as the sale of homes in the West Bank.

The spending cuts have encountered powerful opposition in parliament, even among coalition legislators, who say they will hit lower-income groups hardest. The Treasury is now seeking to find alternatives to its proposed cuts in child allowances and increased fees for physicians visits.
Parliament has until December 31 to approve the 1997 budget. If it fails to pass the spending package by then, the government will operate for up to three months according to the 1996 budget.

The cabinet's decision on Friday to reinstate investment and tax benefits to West Bank settlements will have no impact on the budget, Treasury sources said. West Bank settlers were already entitled to personal income tax reductions, and the renewal of investment subsidies to West Bank factories will come out of the general investment-aid budget.

However, the decision could open a new fissure between the government and Foreign Minister David Levy's Gesher faction in the ruling Likud party which has mounted the strongest fight against the Treasury cuts.
